# Change-Index Mosaic

The change-index mosaic is the common raster foundation for the annual workflow. It is not just a preprocessing artifact. In the current implementation it is the annual raster against which deterministic patches are detected and from which supervised polygon-level features are later derived.

## Methodological Role

The paper draft frames OtsuFire around a burned-sensitive annual change variable derived from pre- and post-fire composites. The package-facing code generalizes that idea as a `change_index`, while the current annual runtime commonly consumes a `MinMin_<year>_mosaic_res90m.tif` mosaic. The book therefore uses `change_index` as the generic term and refers to the MinMin mosaic as the current operational realization of that input.

Because both deterministic and supervised stages depend on the same annual raster reference, errors at the mosaic stage propagate directly into candidate detection, feature extraction, and any downstream validation.

## Current Public Entry Point

The package-facing mosaic function is `change_index_mosaic()`. The current signature supports the following main arguments.

| Argument                    | Current role                                      |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `folder_path`               | Folder containing the annual raster tiles         |
| `mask`                      | AOI mask as `sf`, `SpatVector`, or vector path    |
| `year`                      | Optional explicit year label for output naming    |
| `raster_pattern`            | Pattern used to discover candidate tiles          |
| `output_dir`                | Output location for the final mosaic              |
| `mosaic_name`               | Optional stable name override                     |
| `nodata_value`              | Explicit NoData value for reading and writing     |
| `cap_below` and `lower_cap` | Optional lower-value stabilization before writing |
| `method`                    | Mosaic strategy: `merge` or `vrt`                 |

Legacy manual usage also still exists under `00_USAGE/00_MOSAIC_USAGE`, but the book uses `change_index_mosaic()` as the current package-facing reference.

## What The Function Verifies Before Mosaicking

The active code performs several checks before writing the annual mosaic.

1.  It discovers candidate tiles from `folder_path` using `raster_pattern`, then excludes files whose basenames already look like mosaics, resampled outputs, or projected outputs.
2.  It checks that all selected tiles have the same band count, CRS, resolution, and grid origin.
3.  It loads the AOI mask and reprojects it to the raster CRS when needed.
4.  It refuses to proceed when any tile is geometrically incompatible with the reference tile.

These checks are important methodologically, not only technically. The supervised pipeline later aligns DOY, delayed-change, topography, slope, and CORINE rasters to the annual change-index template. A weak mosaic stage would therefore destabilize every later polygon-level comparison.

## Assembly Logic

After compatibility checks, the current function either merges the tiles directly or builds a temporary VRT. The assembled raster is then cropped to the AOI extent, masked to the AOI geometry, and optionally stabilized by capping extreme low values below `lower_cap`. The current default is to apply that lower cap when `cap_below = TRUE`.

The final raster is written as a tiled, LZW-compressed GeoTIFF with an explicit NoData flag. Band names are preserved when possible.

## Main Outputs

`change_index_mosaic()` returns a structured summary as well as writing the final raster.

| Output               | Meaning                                                                           |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `mosaic_path`        | Path to the final masked annual GeoTIFF                                           |
| `tile_inventory`     | List of the tiles used to build the mosaic                                        |
| `method_used`        | Whether `merge` or `vrt` was used                                                 |
| `mask_summary`       | Mask source, CRS handling, and reprojection note                                  |
| `mosaic_diagnostics` | Tile count, year label, NoData handling, lower-cap settings, and output directory |
| `temporary_vrt`      | Path to the temporary VRT when that option is retained                            |

## Downstream Use In The Annual Workflow

The deterministic runtime resolves the annual mosaic as `one_year_tif` and uses it as the raster input to Otsu thresholding, growth, refinement, and later RBR-based support scoring. The supervised runtime uses the same annual raster as its main `change_index`, and then aligns delayed-change, DOY, DEM, slope, and CORINE layers to that same raster geometry before feature extraction.

In practice, this means the mosaic is not merely an input file. It is the spatial reference system for the full annual workflow.

## Minimal Package-Facing Example

``` r
res <- change_index_mosaic(
  folder_path = "C:/path/to/annual_tiles",
  mask = "C:/path/to/aoi_mask.shp",
  year = 2025,
  raster_pattern = "S2_sev_AUTUMN_mean_mean_2025_tile*.tif",
  output_dir = "C:/path/to/output",
  lower_cap = -1000,
  method = "merge"
)
```

::: callout-note
The paper draft describes the annual burned-sensitive raster mainly in RBR terms, whereas the current package-facing API uses the more general term `change_index`. That wording difference is intentional in this book: the methodology is burned-sensitive spectral change, and the active annual runtime currently instantiates it with the MinMin mosaic.
:::
